subject: Bypassing ctmm.select and using a specific model

messages.author: dd91502c6a6e8586
messages.subject: Bypassing ctmm.select and using a specific model
parts:
Hi Dr. Fleming,

I want to do some new analyses on data I've already run in ctmm before - top models for all individuals were OUF. I'm trying to avoid running ctmm.select again, since it will take days to fit models for my individuals, but my understanding is that the selection process is what can give me the modeled data as an object.

Is there a bypass here so I can jump straight to the AKDE function using only OUF? I've tried - no success. I thought I saw a previous post about this but now I can't find it for the life of me.

Thank you,
Laura (PhD student)

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Bypassing ctmm.select and using a specific model
parts:
Hi Laura,

If you happen to know the best model, then you can use ctmm.fit() to fit that one model.
Also, I recommend saving the fit objects after running ctmm.select(), as they take the longest to calculate and take up very little space.

Best,
Chris

Thank you so much, Chris! I appreciate it. 

While I was puttering around trying to troubleshoot, I moved over to ctmmweb for a bit and it is fabulous! Everything seemed to work well except my attempt to export home range shapefiles. Despite some Google searches and troubleshooting, I have continuously gotten the error message:

Error in .local: no slot of name "pnt" for this object of class "SpatVector"
2: shiny::runApp
1. ctmmweb::web

I tried taking it out of parallel mode to see if that would change anything (no dice), but based on my limited web findings, it might have something to do with my version of r versus my version of web browser? I saw on the ctmmweb documentation that Chrome is recommended; however, I have switched to FireFox since reports came out that Google started mining more personal information from Chrome. I could re-download Chrome if it is just an issue of the browser.

Sincerely,
Laura
